narrative.overview: Null looks like a cold, clinical examination room for trading strategies. The interface is a dark navy slab lit from within; the user brings a strategy they believe in, and the tool lays it out, cuts into it, and reports what it finds — without sentiment. The serif carries the gravity of a verdict; the monospace is the instrument readout clicking off real measurements; the single neon-lime accent is the one live signal on an otherwise lightless slab. The system is restrained to the point of austerity — no gloss, no gradient buttons, no drop shadows, no decorative illustration. Depth comes entirely from tonal navy layering and hairline borders. Color is almost entirely withheld so that when it does appear it means something: lime for what survives scrutiny, amber for what is shaky, red for what is dead. The anti-reference is the hype-driven retail trading app.
keyCharacteristics: Dark navy "examination slab" canvas; depth by tonal layering, never shadow.
Three-voice typography: serif judgment, mono measurement, sans explanation.
One reserved accent (neon lime) carrying semantic weight, never decoration.
A traffic-light semantic palette (lime / amber / red) tied to verdict severity.
Numbers are always monospace and tabular — measurements, not marketing.

rules.name: The One Signal Rule
rules.body: Signal Lime appears on no more than a small fraction of any screen. It is the live wire — a CTA, the logo, a focus ring, a surviving metric. If lime is everywhere, nothing reads as the signal.

rules.name: The Color-Means-Severity Rule
rules.body: Lime / amber / red are never aesthetic choices. They are bound to meaning: good / caution / fatal. Never color for decoration.

rules.name: The Numbers Are Mono Rule
rules.body: Every computed figure is JetBrains Mono with tabular-nums. Numbers are instrument output and must align in columns like a readout; never set in the serif or the sans.

rules.name: The Serif Speaks Only to Judge Rule
rules.body: Newsreader is reserved for verdicts, headlines, and the italic gloss. It carries weight precisely because it is scarce.

rules.name: The No-Shadow Rule
rules.body: Surfaces never cast shadows. If something must separate from its background, it does so with a tonal step and a hairline border — not a shadow.

dos: Do keep Signal Lime rare and meaningful — a CTA, the logo, a focus ring, a surviving metric — never a background or a decorative flourish (The One Signal Rule).
Do set every computed number in JetBrains Mono with tabular-nums, colored by severity (lime good / bone neutral / red bad).
Do build depth from tonal navy layering (Abyss → Slab → Raised) plus 1px Hairline borders.
Do reserve Newsreader serif for verdicts, headlines, and the italic gloss.
Do give every interactive element the 2px Signal Lime :focus-visible outline, and honor prefers-reduced-motion.
donts: Don't add box-shadows or faux-3D elevation — the system is flat by doctrine (The No-Shadow Rule).
Don't use lime, amber, or red decoratively; each is bound to a severity meaning.
Don't import hype-trading-app tropes — gradient CTAs, confetti, gamified dopamine, green/red candle decoration, "to the moon" energy.
Don't set numbers in the serif or sans, and don't use the serif for UI chrome or body copy.
Don't soften a DEAD/SHAKY verdict visually; it is color-coded honestly and presented at full size — the kill is the tool working.
